messages:
Devon: customer 'BrightFlow' opened a support ticket — they get intermittent 429s even though they have org credits and a Dedicated quota. Happens across multiple projects. stack: frontend -> proxy -> our API.

Ava: thanks Devon. any customer correlation ids or sample request ids?

Devon: sent IDs in the ticket: req=bf-20260205-7a3c, req=bf-20260205-9b1f. They say it mostly hits during morning batch windows.

Maya: quick hypothesis: looks like quota enforcement at request scope (api-key or project) + IP-based burst gating at the edge proxy. If proxy is pooling requests from many projects under one egress IP, IP throttle might trigger even if org-level quota remains.

Ibrahim: @Maya yeah we saw similar with another customer when a shared proxy aggregated calls. Our rate limiter has these dimensions: org_id, project_id, api_key, and source_ip. Limits fall back in that order for enforcement reporting.

Devon: customer insists they used the org API key in multiple projects, expecting shared quota. They have billing credits applied to org.

Maya: sending what to check: 1) which API key was used on those failed requests (check Authorization header) 2) X-Forwarded-For on proxy 3) rate-limit response headers we returned (x-rw-limit-*, x-rw-retry-after).

Ava: I looked at the two request IDs — both used api_key 'bf-org-primary' but the proxy rewrites Authorization sometimes when routing to internal project tokens. The logs show original_key=b'bf-org-primary' and routed_key=b'bf-proj-9' in proxy metadata.

Devon: so proxy is swapping keys? customer says they never created per-project keys.

Ibrahim: that's our proxy config for multi-tenant customers that want per-service keys — it can optionally inject a project key. For BrightFlow it looks like an old deploy had inject_project_key: true. That explains the auth mismatch.

Maya: consequence: requests were authenticated as proj-9 for quota checks, but billing credit is applied at org-level only. The project-level quota hit triggered 429s while org credit remained.

Devon: can we confirm rate-limit headers on the failed responses?

Ava: yes captured: \n```\nHTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nx-rw-limit-type: project\nx-rw-limit-window: 60\nx-rw-limit-remaining: 0\nx-rw-retry-after: 18\nx-rw-quota-id: proj-9\n```\n
Maya: that nails it. Also saw edge logs with source_ip 34.122.11.77 — this IP shows bursts from other tenants during same window; edge IP-based smoothing kicked in as well (we have an IP-level short-window cap to protect noisy neighbors).

Ibrahim: remediation options: (A) turn off proxy inject_project_key so requests use org key (B) create a dedicated API key per project and expand project quota, (C) request temporary bump for proj-9 while customer fixes proxy.

Devon: customer asked for immediate fix — they prefer not to change their proxy config themselves.

Ava: short-term we can: 1) apply a temporary project quota override for proj-9 for 1 hour to absorb backlog, 2) add an IP override to raise the burst cap for 34.122.11.77 for 2 hours. Both require infra action.

Ibrahim: I can apply the IP burst override (I have a runbook). For project quota override I need approvals for emergency quota changes — passing to @Maya for product approval.

Maya: approve temporary quota increase + reduce enforcement priority on IP cap for that IP for two hours. Leave audit notes. :white_check_mark:

DeployBot: runbook-exec: ip-burst-override --ip 34.122.11.77 --window 10s --limit 1200 => started by Ibrahim at 2026-02-05T15:37:12Z

Ibrahim: applied the IP override, monitoring now.

Ava: I pushed a one-hour project quota bump to proj-9 (50% more tokens) and added a note for support audit.

Devon: can we give the customer a clear recommended long-term fix?

Maya: yes: 1) stop proxy injecting project keys unless they intend project-scoped quotas 2) if they want isolation, provision separate API keys per project and set appropriate project quotas + link billing to org credits via console (we have docs) 3) add metrics alerting on x-rw-limit-type:project 4) consider using our Dedicated capacity for stable throughput.

Ava: sending sample repro curl for their infra team to test after proxy change:\n```\ncurl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer bf-org-primary" \\\n  -H "X-Forwarded-For: 34.122.11.77" \\\n  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'\n```\n
Devon: customer confirmed 429s stopped after we applied overrides. They're going to schedule a proxy rollout to disable inject_project_key.

Maya: follow-ups: Ibrahim to remove IP override in 2 hours, Ava to revert project quota bump after 1 hour, Devon to confirm customer proxy change and close ticket.

Ibrahim: noted, will remove override at 17:40Z unless asked to extend.

Ava: logging action items in ticket and adding links to docs: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/rate-limits and https://console.redwood.ai/docs/key-management :memo:

Devon: customer very appreciative. closing loop once proxy change is deployed. :smile:

SRE-bot: incident-note: temporary quota and IP override applied for BrightFlow (proj-9). Audit-id: ao-20260205-7782

Maya: thanks everyone. Good catch on the proxy key rewrite. Learned: shared egress IP + key rewriting = sneaky project scoping bug. :+1:
